text.p: Europe's largest mobile phone maker Nokia on Monday said a record second-quarter helped its first-half profit surge to 3.33 billion markka, and said it had reason to maintain an outlook for good full-year profitability.
Analysts polled by Reuters had expected Nokia's profit over the period to rise strongly from a weak year-ago level of 1.13 billion, to about three billion markka, in a 2.97-3.3 billion markka range.
The company said net sales bounded to 24.39 billion markka from the weak 16.88 billion year-ago level, and earnings per share climbed to 8.49 markka from 2.97.
It said mobile phone sales rose 49 percent and its sales of telecoms infrastructure "clearly surpassed market growth" by rising 35 percent.

"The results meet our performance targets and give us reason to maintain our previously stated positive outlook for strong growth and good profitability for the whole year," it said in a statement with the results.
Nokia's stock in Helsinki picked up from an earlier unchanged level shortly after the news, trading up 4.50 markka at 477 some 20 minutes after the news.
Before the report it had touched a new year-high of 485.00 markka, tracking a sharp rise in its New York-listed ADR on Friday.

Nokia's report came as expectations had ratcheted up sharply after a surprise 44 percent surge in H1 profit last month from Swedish rival Ericsson, which put in very fast growth in mobile handsets and benefited from currency gains.
